title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
statement:
You receive two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, each sorted in non-decreasing order, and an integer `k`. A pair `[u, v]` combines one entry `u` of `nums1` with one entry `v` of `nums2`; pairs formed from different positions are different pairs, even when their values coincide. Return a list of `k` such pairs whose sums `u + v` are the smallest possible: no pair left out may have a smaller sum than a pair you return. `k` never exceeds `nums1.length * nums2.length`.

When several pairs share the sum at the cutoff, any of them may be chosen, and the pairs may be listed in any order.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 are each sorted in non-decreasing order
signature: List<List<Integer>> kSmallestPairs(int[] nums1, int[] nums2, int k)
notes:
## Intuition

Listing all `nums1.length * nums2.length` pairs and sorting them works, but it is far too slow when both arrays are long. Because both arrays are sorted, think of the pairs as a grid where row `i` uses `nums1[i]` and column `j` uses `nums2[j]`: sums only grow to the right along a row. So each row only needs its leftmost unused pair as a candidate, and a min-heap of those candidates always holds the next smallest pair.

## Approach

1. For each of the first `min(nums1.length, k)` rows, push the entry `[nums1[i] + nums2[0], i, 0]` into the min-heap `heap` (rows past `k` can never contribute).
2. While `result` has fewer than `k` pairs, pop the entry with the smallest sum and append `[nums1[i], nums2[j]]`.
3. If that row has another column, push its next candidate `[nums1[i] + nums2[j + 1], i, j + 1]`.
4. Return `result`.

`push` and `pop` are a standard binary heap ordered by the sum stored at index 0 of each entry.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums1 = [1, 7, 11]`, `nums2 = [2, 4, 6]`, `k = 3`. The heap starts with sums 3 (row 0), 9 (row 1) and 13 (row 2).

- Pop 3, add `[1, 2]`, push row 0's next sum `1 + 4 = 5`.
- Pop 5, add `[1, 4]`, push `1 + 6 = 7`.
- Pop 7, add `[1, 6]`; row 0 is exhausted.

`result` has 3 pairs: `[[1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 6]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(k log m) with m = min(nums1.length, k): the heap never holds more than m entries and we pop at most k times.
- Space: O(m) for the heap, plus the k pairs returned.

## Pitfalls

- Seeding every row of a huge `nums1` wastes time; only the first `k` rows matter.
- Pushing both the right and the lower neighbour of a popped cell creates duplicates unless you track visited cells; seeding column 0 of every row avoids that.
- Stop after `k` pairs, and remember equal values at different positions are separate pairs.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | min-heap of `[sum, i, j]` candidates, one per active row |
| `push`, `pop` | insert into and remove the minimum from `heap` |
| `i`, `j` | row index into `nums1` and column index into `nums2` |
| `result` | the pairs chosen so far, in increasing sum |
